key_insight: Diamond–silicon nitride friction shifts from bond-density-controlled interfacial sliding to shear within the softer material as passivation, crystal orientation and load alter interfacial bonding.
engineering_relevance: The potential enables larger-scale reactive simulations to investigate diamond wear, chemical-mechanical polishing and ceramic interfaces beyond first-principles simulation limits.
method: Train a reactive machine learning potential for C/H/N/O/Si across bulk materials, surfaces, interfaces and environmental molecules.
Test diamond surface reaction barriers and amorphous silicon nitride and silica structural/mechanical properties.
Simulate diamond–silicon nitride sliding across four diamond orientations, clean and H/OH-passivated surfaces, and 0.1–23 GPa normal loads.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports training on a large, diverse structural dataset and evaluation against ab initio reaction barriers and amorphous-material properties, but provides no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Transferability to wear, plowing asperities and silica sliding requires further validation; the reported sliding study focuses on diamond–silicon nitride.
paper_title: Development and application of a machine learning potential for diamond surfaces and their sliding interfaces with silicon nitride and silica: effect of passivation, orientation and load
